summary: Fame Point's 1880 wooden keeper's-house light gave way to a 1907 cast-iron tower, taken to Quebec City in the 1970s and returned in 1997.

structures.note: About 50 ft per Lighthouse Friends and Fallu; Rowlett gives 11 m (36 ft). Light discontinued 1 October 1907.
49 ft from base to vane per the 1908 Department report (Fallu gives 15.5 m). Taken down 1977 or 1978, returned 1997.
Coast Guard light nearby; Rowlett gives 31 m in the Fame Point entry and 33 m in the 1975 entry. Listed as active.

access.note: Heritage site open in season; 4.3 km dirt road with a steep grade from Route 132 (Lighthouse Friends).

facts.agency: Comité local de développement de L'Anse-à-Valleau

events.note: Parliament appropriated $4,000 for the light (Lighthouse Friends; Fallu gives the amount without a date)
Light first shown October 1880 (station history page says 1 October); keeper James Ascah appointed 2 September 1880
Hamilton-Foster siren in operation 8 October 1902
SS Monteagle ran onto Serpent Reef, 7 miles east of Fame Point, early on 12 July 1902
Tower painted red on 1 July 1903, as an experiment (previously white with black band)
Marconi wireless station finished 25 June 1904; first contact with the outbound Allan liner Parisian
New fog-alarm building with diaphone machinery, built 1905-1906; 212-ton coal shed and 50 ft brick stack added
Cast-iron tower built by day labour; put in operation 1 October 1907 when the old light was discontinued
First-order double flashing light in operation at the point
Canadian army camp and huts set up on the point during the First World War (1914-1918)
SS Nicoya torpedoed by U-553 off Cloridorme, night of 11-12 May 1942; survivors landed at L'Anse-à-Valleau
Radio station operations ended; moved 26 km east to Rivière-au-Renard
Historic 1907 tower light discontinued; Coast Guard light on a skeletal tower nearby
Coast Guard light on a skeletal tower (Rowlett lists it as active)
Tower dismantled and moved to Quebec City: 1977 per Rowlett, the station history page and the 2017 bulletin; 1978 per Fallu
Tower reassembled in front of the Coast Guard headquarters in the Old Port of Quebec
Tower returned to the point; ceremony 3 November 1997 (Fallu)
Marconi radio station rebuilt on the point
Keeper's house rebuilt outside to the appearance of the first (1880) lighthouse
Cited as a municipal historic monument (cité) by the City of Gaspé
Commission des lieux et monuments historiques du Canada commemorated the national historic importance of the maritime radiotelegraph system here

keepers.name: James Ascah
keepers.note: First keeper; appointed 2 September 1880 (keepers' table); also telegraph operator and signal man. The Musée archive gives his life dates as 1830-1915 and places his son Bert's succession at his death, so the end of his service is disputed.

keepers.name: Bert Ascah
keepers.note: Musée de la Gaspésie archive: took over the light on the death of his father James; life dates 1884-1963. The archive does not say whether he is the same man as Hubert Leigh Ascah; not joined to that line.

keepers.name: Hubert Leigh Ascah
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends: 1913 to at least 1936. The 1914 report's table prints H. L. Ascah (OCR 'H. L, Ascah') on the printed row for Fame point, light and fog alarm; checked on the page image. A new keeper's dwelling was built in 1926 during his keepership.

keepers.name: Yvon Élément
keepers.note: Last keeper; left his post in 1975 (Fallu; bulletin). Connection ended 1975, so named only in the published role.

wrecks.outcome: Ran onto Serpent Reef, 7 miles east of Fame Point, at about 2.35 a.m. The Department's inquiry found that the second mate had altered course towards the shore. Came off 17 July, went to Montreal to discharge, then to New York for repairs.

Torpedoed by U-553 off Cloridorme, night of 11-12 May 1942; six crew died (Mathurin). Survivors were brought ashore at L'Anse-à-Valleau. The keeper's report counted 49 survivors, per Mathurin's footnote; Fallu says nearly fifty. The station passed news of the sinking to the military.

corrections.proposed: historic 1907 tower inactive since 1975; a Coast Guard light on a skeletal tower nearby is listed as active
corrections.why: Rowlett's entries put the historic light out in 1975 and a 1975 Coast Guard light on a separate skeletal tower as active. The record's inactive status describes only the historic tower. Needs a check against the Canadian Coast Guard List of Lights before any change.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's 1907 date is the discontinuation of the 1880 tower's light, when the 1907 tower was lit (Department report). The 1975 date is when the 1907 tower's light was discontinued (Lighthouse Friends, Fallu, Rowlett).

notes_for_editor: Keepers: the James Ascah service end is disputed. LF, Fallu and the 2017 bulletin give 1880 to 1913; the Musée archive gives James's life as 1830-1915 and has his son Bert (1884-1963) succeed him on his death. Bert and Hubert Leigh Ascah may or may not be one man; kept as separate lines, not joined. Checked on the page images: the 1914 table (1915 volume, scan p. 70, printed p. 63) has the printed row 'Fame point, light and fog alarm' with H. L. Ascah on it, so the link is by the printed row, not by column position alone. The image also shows an appointment date of 1 Feb 1913 and salary 1,200.00; the OCR does not carry that date, so it is not footnoted. The 1901 keepers' table row (1901 volume, scan p. 221, printed p. 124, 'Between Montreal and Quebec and below Quebec') reads 'Ascah, James, Fame Point, Gaspe Co, September 2, 1880' on the image. The Monteagle distance prints as '7^ miles' in the OCR; the story says seven miles, as the wreck record does, and does not quote the caret. The bulletin's 'depuis l964' is OCR for 1964. Dimensions: the 1880 tower is about 50 ft in LF and Fallu but 36 ft in Rowlett; the 1907 tower is 49 ft to the vane in the report, 15.5 m in Fallu and the bulletin, 49 ft in Rowlett. Range: the 1908 report says 'twenty miles' with no unit; Fallu gives 83 km and the bulletin 80 km. range_nm is left unset because the unit is not stated. Dates: removal to Quebec City is 1977 (Rowlett, station page, bulletin) or 1978 (Fallu); kept as disputed. Modern light: Rowlett's 1975 Coast Guard light is marked active; not checked against the CCG List of Lights, so the status correction is proposed, not made. Position: the record's OSM point (49.108498, -64.601811) is about 100 m from LF and Rowlett (49.1083, -64.6003); not corrected. Not used: the station page's Champlain names (Cap Lévesque 1613, Cap de la Boutonnière 1625) could not be checked; the Erudit 2018 article on the Ascah family (Anubis-protected) was not read and was not bypassed; the Poirier 2005 'Historique' booklet (cited by the Musée) and the 2021 Le Soleil article were not read. The log book: the Fallu note gives the log title as 'July 20, 1904 to 1915' while the first entry is dated 25 June 1904; the original was not seen (quoted second-hand). Nicoya: the 49 survivors figure is second-hand via Mathurin's footnote; the keeper's report itself is outside the corpus (1942). Living people: no private individuals named; the local fishermen and the 1992-1997 committee women are unnamed in the sources; Élément is named only in the keeper role.
